findings.text: Creation or lookup of a System V shared segment is requested with a key plus size plus flags. A thin system call wrapper forwards to a kernel helper that resolves the caller namespace, packages the three inputs, and invokes a shared IPC lookup routine parametrized by a creation callback plus an association callback plus an extra size check.

Creation rejects a size below the documented minimum or above the per namespace maximum, rejects cases where rounding up to pages would wrap below the requested size, and rejects cases where adding pages would wrap the namespace total or exceed the namespace total allowance. The first class reports invalid argument while overflow and allowance failures report no space, with no durable state changed.

A successfully published segment has mode limited to permission bits, a valid security association, a backing file whose reserve treatment reflects huge versus ordinary choice and overcommit configuration, creation time set with access and detach times cleared, zero initial attaches, current task as creator with list linkage, namespace totals charged, and backing inode number equal to the assigned identifier within the namespace limit.

If identifier insertion fails after backing store creation, creator and last process references are cleared, the file reference is dropped, and the descriptor is released through a reference drop path. If backing store setup fails earlier, the descriptor including its security state is released through a deferred callback without touching namespace totals or creator linkage.

When an existing identifier matches the requested key, the additional validation accepts only if the stored segment size is at least the requested size, otherwise it fails with invalid argument and leaves the existing segment unchanged.

Lookup with locking starts under read side protection, resolves the identifier, acquires the object lock, then revalidates that the object was not concurrently removed. A removed object is unlocked and reported as removed identifier, an unresolvable identifier propagates its lookup error with protection released, and success returns a locked descriptor with read side protection still held for the caller to release after unlocking. A by pointer variant acquires the same two protections without lookup, assuming the caller already holds a reference.

Detach paths that may destroy hold the namespace read write semaphore in write mode across the whole lookup plus object locked section, while the orphan scan that only inspects destroy eligibility holds just the object lock after checking creator linkage. Task exit never holds task lock together with namespace or object locks, it unlinks under task lock, releases that lock, then acquires namespace and object locks for conditional destruction.

The creator back pointer is trustworthy only while the creator list node is non empty under read side protection. Removal checks emptiness, then under the creator task lock performs an idempotent delete initialization that tolerates a concurrent exit path having already unlinked the same node.

Attachment open validates the stored file identity after locking, mismatch indicates identifier reuse and fails without changing accounting. On match it stamps access time, records the caller thread group as last attacher, and increments the attach count. Detach stamps detach time plus last attacher, decrements the count, then destroys when eligible else unlocks, always under namespace write protection.

Virtual area open and close first invoke any underlying open or close handler, then adjust attach accounting through the shared open and close paths, warning once if the identifier raced with lookup or destruction. Fault delegates unconditionally, while split and page size and policy operations delegate when the underlying handler exists and otherwise use neutral defaults of success, base page size, or current policy.

Mapping first performs attachment accounting so a removed or reused identifier fails before any mapping, then maps the backing file and on mapping failure undoes the accounting. On success it saves the resulting underlying area operations and installs the shared memory area operations. Release drops the namespace reference and backing file reference, clears the file association, and frees the wrapper.

Synchronization plus allocation plus unmapped area selection are forwarded to the backing file operations. Missing synchronization reports invalid argument, missing allocation reports operation not supported, and unmapped selection assumes the backing handler exists.

Two file operation tables expose mapping plus synchronization plus release plus unmapped area plus no operation seek plus allocation, with the huge variant additionally marked for huge pages. One area operation table exposes open plus close plus fault plus split plus page size, with policy hooks present only under non uniform memory builds.

The kernel segment descriptor contains permission state shm_perm and namespace ns and creator shm_creator with linkage shm_clist and backing file shm_file and size shm_segsz and attach count shm_nattch and times shm_atim plus shm_dtim plus shm_ctim and process markers shm_cprid plus shm_lprid and accounting mlock_ucounts. Mode inside permission state carries destroy marking SHM_DEST tested for eligibility.

The per open wrapper associates a namespace ns with an identifier id plus a backing file file plus saved area operations vm_ops. Each task carries inside sysvshm a head collecting creator nodes shm_clist, with new descriptors added under task lock and removed either by exit drain or by creator unlink.

Task exit repeatedly takes the task lock, stops when the creator list is empty, otherwise peeks the first descriptor and remembers its namespace which outlives the descriptor. When forced removal is disabled it only unlinks the node and continues for later cleanup. When enabled it pins the namespace when possible else only unlinks, then pins the descriptor, unlinks last under task lock, releases that lock, then under namespace write protection plus object lock plus reference drop it destroys when eligible and valid, else merely unlocks, handling already removed objects by unlock only.

The orphan scan callback skips any descriptor whose creator linkage remains non empty. For fully orphaned entries it acquires the object lock by pointer and then either destroys when eligible or unlocks, always reporting success to continue iteration.

Destruction eligibility requires zero attaches together with either namespace wide forced removal enabled or the destroy marker present in permission mode. Attach count may change under object lock alone without namespace protection, so eligibility must be tested only while holding the object lock.

Privileged control for removal and permission update executes under namespace write protection plus read side protection, after resolving and validating the target with permission checks and security authorization. Removal transfers to a dedicated removal helper that releases object and outer protections, while permission update refreshes change time on success. Other operation codes fail as invalid argument.

Information queries report namespace limits plus highest index for the generic variant, and additionally usage counts plus resident plus swapped totals plus namespace page total with swap attempt counters fixed at zero for the detailed variant. Status queries support positional lookup for Linux extensions and checked lookup for the standard command, with one extension auditing without traditional read permission checks while others require read access. Standard status returns zero on success while Linux extensions return the full identifier including sequence.

Status filling zeroes the output buffer, holds read side protection across lookup, performs audit or permission plus security checks before taking the object lock, revalidates after locking and reports removed identifier if torn down, then exports permission state plus size plus three timestamps with high halves on non sixty four bit builds plus numeric creator and last process identifiers plus attach count.

The observed prefix of the lock or unlock control path performs checked lookup under read side protection, audits the object, authorizes through security, acquires the object lock, and bails as removed identifier when revalidation shows concurrent teardown. The remainder of the path beyond that check is not present in the routed fragment.

Descriptor copying supports a native sixty four bit layout copied verbatim and a legacy layout translating permission plus size plus times plus process identifiers plus attach count, while legacy input copies only owner plus group plus mode. Information copying likewise supports both layouts with clamping of maximum size to signed maximum in legacy output. Unknown versions fail as invalid argument and user copy faults propagate as faults.

Resident and swap accounting distinguishes huge backing by scaling mapping page count by pages per huge page, ordinary shmem by adding mapping pages plus swapped count under inode lock when shmem support exists, and a fallback adding only mapping pages otherwise. Namespace totals are gathered by walking the identifier table from zero up to the in use count while skipping empty slots.

Identifier reuse is detected by comparing the locked descriptor backing file against the opener backing file, with mismatch treated as invalid without accounting change. Lookup races with removal or destruction are treated as busted identifiers and reported once through a warning helper. Deferred freeing releases security state before freeing the container, and callers must validate error pointers from locking helpers before dereference.

Two small lookup helpers wrap unchecked positional resolution and checked identifier resolution respectively, propagating lookup errors unchanged and otherwise converting the generic permission pointer to the enclosing segment descriptor.

Making an identifier private first removes its key from the hash and then marks its key as private. Boot initialization registers the shared memory proc interface with a column header whose width differs between thirty two bit and wider builds, and initializes plus publishes the initial IPC namespace.

Observed ABI vocabulary includes private key IPC_PRIVATE and destroy marking SHM_DEST and minimum size SHMMIN, control codes IPC_RMID plus IPC_SET plus IPC_STAT plus IPC_INFO plus SHM_INFO plus SHM_STAT plus SHM_STAT_ANY, version selectors IPC_64 plus IPC_OLD, creation flags SHM_HUGETLB plus SHM_NORESERVE with huge size selector built from shift SHM_HUGE_SHIFT and mask SHM_HUGE_MASK, permission masks S_IRWXUGO plus S_IRUGO, and base page size PAGE_SIZE.
